narrative.overview: KNOuX looks like a precision instrument mounted in a dark workshop. The ground is near-black graphite, the surfaces rise in three measurable steps, and colour is never decoration: violet is the brand and the selection signal, and every other hue is bound to a state. A screen is correct when a non-technical owner can read it in one glance and a technician can audit every number on it. Density is the default: hairline rules, tabular figures and aligned columns carry the information instead of nested cards.
keyCharacteristics: Midnight graphite ground with three explicit surface steps; no fourth level.
Violet is identity and selection; the other four hues are state, never mood.
Hairline rules and aligned columns instead of nested panels.
Tabular figures wherever a number can be compared.
Real Windows artefacts are the only permitted imagery.
Every unmeasured value declares itself as unmeasured.

rules.name: The State-Colour Rule
rules.body: A hue other than violet appears only when it means something. If the reason is aesthetic, the answer is quiet ink.

rules.name: The Honest Blank Rule
rules.body: An unknown value is rendered as an em dash at half opacity, not as zero, not as "N/A", and not as a friendly sentence repeated down a column.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number a user can compare across rows is set in tabular figures.

rules.name: The One-Display Rule
rules.body: A screen has exactly one 28px display line. A second one means two worlds are competing for the same viewport.

rules.name: The One-Inset-Rule
rules.body: A selected row is marked by inset 3px 0 0 in the world hue, mirrored to the inline end in RTL. Selection never changes the row's height.

dos: Do bind each world to one hue through [data-world] and let it own a distinct composition, not a distinct palette.
Do source every visible number, icon and status from a verified local Windows provider, and render an em dash when the provider did not answer.
Do keep the head band under roughly 180px at 1366x768 so the ledger shows at least eight rows above the fold.
Do put a consequence in a control's label: what will change, and whether it can be undone.
Do test each screen at 1920x1080, 1366x768 and 860x600, in Arabic RTL and English LTR, in dark and light.
donts: Don't present an unimplemented command as functional.
Don't use nested cards, gradient text, eyebrow headings, or a decorative glow on data.
Don't ship invented imagery: no fake sparklines, no rings around numbers that are not ratios, no downloaded or guessed application logos.
Don't let a control's width be decided by its longest Windows string.
Don't repeat a sentence such as "Not recorded" down a column.
